messages:
jane (acme-app): Hey team — migrating our tool-calling flow from OpenAI -> Redwood and hitting schema validation errors. Calls to /v1/functions return 400: 'priority' not a valid enum. Example request + response below, anyone seen this? cc @redwood-support

jane (acme-app): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/functions/run -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "name": "create_ticket",
  "arguments": { "title": "Login failure", "priority": "high" }
}'

jane (acme-app): Response: 400 Bad Request
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Invalid enum value 'high' for field 'priority'",
    "code": "validation_error"
  }
}

maria (support): Hi Jane — thanks for the repro. Can you paste the exact error body and the model/SDK you're calling from? Also are you using any proxy or the Redwood-hosted endpoint directly?

jane (acme-app): Using server->server with node 18, fetch to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/functions. Error body above is verbatim. No proxy. Model: rwd-chat-1. SDK: our in-house wrapper (just posts JSON).

maria (support): Quick heads up: Redwood's OpenAI-compatible tool-calling has some intentional field name and enum normalizations. In this case the platform expects 'urgency' not 'priority', and our enum set is ['low','normal','high'] — looks like your clients send ['low','medium','high'] so 'medium' -> 'normal' mapping is needed.

jane (acme-app): Oof — we have thousands of clients using 'priority' with 'medium'. Changing everyone client-side will take weeks. Is there a compatibility shim we can enable on Redwood?

raj (eng-ml): +1 to Maria. There are two practical approaches: 1) temporary request mapping layer that accepts legacy 'priority' and converts to 'urgency' before validation; 2) a compatibility header that tells the validation service to accept OpenAI-style enums for a transition window. Option 1 is simplest now. Example pseudo code you can drop into a proxy: 

```
# pseudo transform (node/python/pseudocode)
const map = { 'high': 'high', 'medium': 'normal', 'low': 'low', 'urgent': 'high' }
if (body.arguments && body.arguments.priority) {
  body.arguments.urgency = map[body.arguments.priority] || 'normal'
  delete body.arguments.priority
}
```

raj (eng-ml): That will let you keep client code unchanged while the value space is normalized for Redwood validation.

ava (tier2): I'll open RED-2345 to track a built-in compatibility mode for OpenAI toolcalling (enum mapping + legacy field aliases). For the short term Maria, can you provide a lightweight proxy snippet we can host in a support sandbox for Jane?

maria (support): Assigning to myself. Here's a tiny nginx + lua transform snippet you can drop in front of your integration quickly: 

```
# nginx conf fragment (lua)
access_by_lua_block {
  local cjson = require 'cjson'
  ngx.req.read_body()
  local body = ngx.req.get_body_data()
  if body then
    local obj = cjson.decode(body)
    if obj.arguments and obj.arguments.priority then
      local map = { high='high', medium='normal', low='low', urgent='high' }
      obj.arguments.urgency = map[obj.arguments.priority] or 'normal'
      obj.arguments.priority = nil
      ngx.req.set_body_data(cjson.encode(obj))
    end
  end
}
proxy_pass https://api.redwood.ai/v1/functions/run;
```

maria (support): Alternatively, if you can't host a proxy, set header `X-Redwood-Compat: openai-toolcall=1` and DM me — we can enable a temporary relax rule on your account while we track the long-term solution.

jane (acme-app): I spun up the nginx transform in our staging and retried — success! No 400s anymore. One follow-up: tool selection behavior changed too — our code relied on returned field 'tool_id' but Redwood uses 'name' for function selection, so some of our handlers aren't matching.

raj (eng-ml): Right — OpenAI and Redwood differ in the canonical tool manifest fields. Best practice: include both when possible. For responses you can normalize like: 

```
// response normalization (pseudo)
if (resp.tool_id and not resp.name) resp.name = resp.tool_id
// or build a selection priority: prefer resp.name then resp.tool_id
```

raj (eng-ml): If your runtime picks tools by 'name', make sure the tool manifest presented to the model includes the same 'name' values. We can also add a transient mapping on our end but that gets tricky for rollouts.

jane (acme-app): Thanks — adding the normalization in our handler fixed the tool routing. Rolling this to prod with the nginx proxy as a stopgap. Really appreciate the quick help :raised_hands: 

maria (support): Glad it worked. I've marked this thread as 'monitoring' and will keep RED-2345 open for compatibility improvements. If you want the temporary header toggle enabled for your prod key, DM me the account id and I'll flip it.

jane (acme-app): Will do. Closing from our side after one more smoke test.

maria (support): Thanks — resolving here but leave a note if anything reappears. :white_check_mark:
